prompt: Employee.java is provided and complete. Finish Manager.java, a subclass whose pay() adds a bonus, and Payroll.java, whose static methods total and compare pay() across a mixed Employee[] array polymorphically.
explanation: Manager extends Employee, reuses the superclass constructor through super(...), and overrides pay() to change behavior while keeping the same interface. Payroll never checks what kind of employee it is holding: calling pay() through an Employee reference dispatches to the override at runtime, so polymorphism does the branching for you. Note that Manager cannot touch the private baseSalary field directly and must go through getBaseSalary().
hints: Manager needs its own private double bonus field, assigned in the constructor after the super(name, baseSalary) call.
Override pay() in Manager; use getBaseSalary() (the field in Employee is private) and add the bonus.
In highestPaid, track the best employee seen so far: start with null and replace it whenever pay() is strictly greater.
